correctness.rationale: For k>=2 every collision among four overlapping k-mers forces a period 1, 2 or 3 on a length k+j interval; with 11 forbidden these yield exactly 13 exceptional contexts (six near-long-zero, four alternating, three periodic 001). Their charged probabilities are derived from the uniform global order; the reversed alternating pair cancels in every stationary two-state source. Exact Markov weights give a positive p^k term and a negative [p(1-p)]^{k/3} residue-dependent term; the k=1 boundary is enumerated separately. The sharp sign phase follows from p^3 compared to p(1-p), and the maximal-entropy simplification from the golden-ratio equation. The included standard-library checker independently enumerated 6752 contexts for k<=13 at five rational parameters and checked all 13 exceptional patterns through k=80, including the golden-mean specialization. Conditions, quantifiers, normalization and finite-computation limits are explicit.

originality.rationale: The primary complete text of arXiv:2410.16968 proves generic charged-context identities and explicit densities for iid uniform full shifts; it does not state the Markov source formula or its sharp threshold at the maximal-entropy source. Zheng et al. 2020 also explicitly analyze iid sources, and Yu 2024 studies different hash/filter effects. A related previous claim fixes a lexicographic order instead of averaging uniform global orders, yielding an unrelated parity phenomenon. Searches of published-finding corpus for Markov golden-mean random minimizers and period-three corrections located optimized orders under iid sources, not equivalent or stronger results. The new theorem has a nontrivial parametric phase boundary and does not simply rename a cited result. Unindexed priority is an explicit risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed Markov-weighted minimizer formula could have priority despite the explicit published-finding corpus and literature comparisons
A random fixed global hash order has a source-almost-sure density that need not equal the expectation over random orders; the theorem deliberately claims only the latter
The phase crossover is an asymptotic eventual sign statement for each fixed p, not a uniform-in-p sign bound at finite k

value.rationale: The one-parameter stationary Markov family is a natural correlated-input model for minimizer sketching when adjacent 1s are disallowed. The exact expected sampling cost reveals a genuinely qualitative change: for sticky-zero sources the finite-k excess is positive, for more alternating sources it is eventually negative, and the canonical maximum-entropy source lies precisely at the phase boundary with an exact three-residue law. This is a motivated source-dependent performance invariant and a structural collision-pattern theorem, not a single arbitrary finite computation or mere parameter substitution. No claim about optimal minimizers or real genomic calibration is made.
